answer: A licensed fire lookout tower on a ridge summit gives one applicant one tower for 120 days. The keeper pays a 150 token deposit and a 90 dollar license, then logs ember drift, wind, and smoke at dawn and dusk. A neighbor signs the log weekly, and a ranger climbs the tower twice to check entries against weather notes and burn scars. A forged entry forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper for 180 days. Faking 10,000 towers freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. Like a lighthouse keeper tending one lamp through a storm, a lookout who misses one ember lets the whole slope burn.
